title: Sanofi considering a deal to acquire Insmed, according to report
content: EX-99.1 2 ef20084500_ex99-1.htm EXHIBIT 99.1 Exhibit 99.1 Insmed Reports Third-Quarter 2026 Financial Results and Provides Business Update —Total Company Revenues of $524.4 Million for the Third Quarter of 2026— —BRINSUPRI® (brensocatib) Revenues of $400.1 Million for the Third Quarter of 2026, Reflecting 29% Growth Over the Second Quarter of 2026— —ARIKAYCE® (amikacin liposome inhalation suspension) Revenues of $124.4 Million for the Third Quarter of 2026, Reflecting 9% Growth Over the Third Quarter of 2025— —Company Raises 2026 BRINSUPRI Revenue Guidance to $1.35 Billion to $1.4 Billion— —Company Raises 2026 ARIKAYCE Revenue Guidance to $460 Million to $470 Million— — Insmed Launches BRINSUPRI Tablets 25 mg (brensocatib hydrate) for the Treatment of Non-Cystic Fibrosis Bronchiectasis in Japan— BRIDGEWATER, N.J., October 29, 2026 — Insmed Incorporated (Nasdaq: INSM), a people-first global biopharmaceutical company striving to deliver first- and best-in-class therapies to transform the lives of patients facing serious diseases, today reported financial results for the third quarter ended September 30, 2026, and provided a business update. “The third quarter marked another period of meaningful progress, defined by commercial momentum, regulatory achievements, and advancement across our diversified pipeline,” said Will Lewis, Chair and Chief Executive Officer of Insmed. “BRINSUPRI’s U.S. launch continues to exceed expectations and ARIKAYCE continues to grow while in its ninth year on the market. This performance supports our decision to raise the low end of our full-year 2026 revenue guidance for both products. We were also pleased to receive regulatory approval and launch BRINSUPRI in Japan, a profound milestone for patients living with bronchiectasis. In addition, the FDA’s acceptance of the sNDA for ARIKAYCE in MAC lung disease represents an important step toward expanding access to this therapy for eligible patients, including those that are newly diagnosed or facing recurrent infections. As we advance our Phase 3 TPIP programs across four large indications and progress our early-stage pipeline, we remain focused on delivering meaningful innovation and improving the lives of patients with serious diseases.” Progress and Anticipated Milestones by Therapeutic Area: Respiratory BRINSUPRI • BRINSUPRI global revenue grew 29% in the third quarter of 2026 compared to the second quarter of 2026, driven by strong growth in the U.S. market. • In August 2026, Japan's Ministry of Health, Labour and Welfare (MHLW) approved BRINSUPRI Tablets 25 mg (brensocatib hydrate) for the treatment of non-cystic fibrosis bronchiectasis (NCFB) in adults and pediatric patients 12 years and older. • In October 2026, Insmed launched BRINSUPRI Tablets 25 mg, the first and only MHLW-approved treatment for NCFB, in Japan. 1 ARIKAYCE • ARIKAYCE global revenue grew 9% in the third quarter of 2026 compared to the third quarter of 2025, primarily driven by strong growth in international markets. • In September 2026, the U.S. Food and Drug Administration (FDA) accepted Insmed’s Supplemental New Drug Application (sNDA) for review of ARIKAYCE for the treatment of Mycobacterium avium complex (MAC) lung disease as part of a combination antibacterial drug regimen. The FDA granted Priority Review to the sNDA and set a target action date of January 28, 2027, under the Prescription Drug User Fee Act (PDUFA). • Insmed plans to submit data from the Phase 3 ENCORE study to Japan’s Pharmaceuticals and Medical Devices Agency (PMDA) in the fourth quarter of 2026 to support potential ARIKAYCE label expansion to all patients with MAC lung disease. TPIP • Insmed has now enrolled more than 35% of patients in the Phase 3 PALM-ILD study of treprostinil palmitil inhalation powder (TPIP) in patients with pulmonary hypertension associated with interstitial lung disease (PH-ILD) and expects to complete enrollment in the first half of 2028. • In July 2026, Insmed enrolled its first patient in the Phase 3 PALM-PAH study of TPIP in patients with pulmonary arterial hypertension (PAH). • In September 2026, Insmed initiated the Phase 3 PALM-PPF study of TPIP in patients with progressive pulmonary fibrosis (PPF). • Insmed continues to anticipate initiating a Phase 3 study of TPIP in patients with idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis (IPF) in the first half of 2027. INS1148 • Insmed continues to advance a Phase 2 development program for INS1148, initially targeting IPF, with plans to evaluate PPF and other diseases where inhibition of the pro-inflammatory and pro-fibrotic responses mediated by stem cell factor 248 (SCF248) may be beneficial. Immunology & Inflammation INS1033 • In September 2026, the Phase 1 study of INS1033, a dipeptidyl peptidase 1 (DPP1) inhibitor cleared by the FDA for patients with rheumatoid arthritis (RA), began active enrollment of healthy volunteers. Neuro & Other Rare INS1201 • Insmed completed enrollment of the Phase 1 ASCEND clinical study of INS1201, an intrathecally delivered gene therapy for patients with Duchenne muscular dystrophy (DMD). INS1202 • Insmed continues to enroll patients in the Phase 1 ARMOR study of INS1202, an intrathecally delivered gene therapy for patients with amyotrophic lateral sclerosis (ALS). 2 Corporate Updates • In September 2026, Insmed presented five abstracts from across its Respiratory therapeutic area at the European Respiratory Society (ERS) Congress 2026. • In October 2026, Insmed presented data across its respiratory portfolio at the American College of Chest Physicians (CHEST) 2026 Annual Meeting and IDWeek 2026. • In October 2026, Insmed announced the appointment of Paul Hudson, former Chief Executive Officer of Sanofi and Novartis Pharmaceuticals, and Utpal Koppikar, current Chief Financial Officer of Verily Health, to its Board of Directors. Third-Quarter 2026 Financial Results The following table summarizes third-quarter and year-to-date 2026 and 2025 revenues and revenue growth for BRINSUPRI and ARIKAYCE across our commercial regions: INSMED INCORPORATED Revenue by Region (in millions) Three Months Ended September 30, Nine Months Ended September 30, (in millions) 2026 2025 Growth 2026 2025 Growth ARIKAYCE U.S. $ 75.5 $ 74.0 2% $ 208.6 $ 206.9 1% International 48.9 40.3 21% 130.2 107.6 21% Total $ 124.4 $ 114.3 9% $ 338.8 $ 314.5 8% BRINSUPRI U.S. $ 398.1 $ 28.1 NM $ 913.8 $ 28.1 NM International 2.0 - N/A 3.3 - N/A Total $ 400.1 $ 28.1 NM $ 917.1 $ 28.1 NM Total Revenues U.S. $ 473.6 $ 102.0 364% $ 1,122.4 $ 235.0 378% International 50.8 40.3 26% 133.5 107.6 24% Total $ 524.4 $ 142.3 268% $ 1,255.9 $ 342.6 267% • Cost of product revenues (excluding amortization of intangibles) were $78.2 million for the third quarter of 2026, compared to $29.4 million for the third quarter of 2025. The increase in cost of product revenues in the third quarter of 2026 primarily reflects the increase in total product revenues for ARIKAYCE and BRINSUPRI. Cost of product revenues as a percentage of revenues decreased in the third quarter of 2026 due to sales of BRINSUPRI, which has lower manufacturing costs than ARIKAYCE. • Research and development (R&D) expenses were $270.0 million for the third quarter of 2026, compared to $186.4 million for the third quarter of 2025. title: Pfizer, Verismo Strike Licensing Deals to Push CAR T Manufacturing In Vivo
content: Advertisement News|Articles|November 18, 2026 Pfizer, Verismo Strike Licensing Deals to Push CAR T Manufacturing In Vivo Author(s)Nicholas Jacobus Listen0:00 / 0:00 Key Takeaways Verismo’s Pack-IT license supports in vivo engineering of KIR-CAR T cells, positioning the platform for off-the-shelf delivery with potential reductions in time-to-treatment, cost, and access barriers. Multi-chain KIR-CAR design aims to overcome single-chain CAR constraints, seeking durable antitumor activity with minimized off-target toxicity while Synkir-110 and Synkir-310 progress through Phase I. Pfizer secured ex-Greater China rights to three pre-IND in vivo CAR-T autoimmune programs from Starna, plus technology rights spanning inflammation/immunology and oncology, with options for additional compounds. Financial terms include $330 million upfront and up to $2.3 billion milestones plus royalties, while Pfizer controls ex-China clinical development, U.S. initial manufacturing, and commercialization. The transaction exemplifies large-pharma licensing of China-origin innovation after sustained national investment shifting from low-cost supply to advanced biopharma R&D.SHOW MORE Verismo Therapeutics licenses in vivo CAR T engineering technology from Stanford Medicine, while Pfizer licenses in vivo CAR-T programs from Starna Therapeutics. Advertisement A pair of licensing agreements this week pushed CAR T cell therapy into new territory, with two companies moving to engineer T cells directly inside the body rather than relying on today’s weeks-long manufacturing process.Verismo Therapeutics licenses in vivo CAR T technologyVerismo Therapeutics entered an agreement to license the Pack-it technology enabling in vivo engineering of KIR-CAR T cells from Stanford Medicine. The agreement provides Verismo with technology from the lab of Crystal Mackall, MD, Ernest and Amelia Gallo Family professor, professor of pediatrics and medicine at Stanford Medicine, and founding director of the Stanford Center for Cancer Cell Therapy.1The deal will allow Verismo to extend its multi-chain KIR-CAR platform into next-generation in vivo delivery of KIR-CAR T cell therapies, with the potential to reduce time-to-treatment and cost and broaden patient access over time.1 Verismo’s platform is designed to take CAR T therapy beyond the single-chain limitations of current approaches, with the potential to deliver durable anti-tumor responses while minimizing off-target toxicity. The platform is currently advancing in two Phase I clinical trials: Synkir-110 in solid tumors and Synkir-310 in B-cell malignancies.1 Both trials have generated early positive signals presented at the American Association for Cancer Research 2026 Annual Meeting. Kim continued, saying, "Today, KIR-CAR is advancing along the established CAR T pathway in two Phase 1 clinical trials, and adding the Pack-IT technology is intended to extend the platform into next-generation, off-the-shelf in vivo delivery, realizing the full potential of KIR-CAR to reach more patients, faster, and at lower cost."Pfizer licenses in vivo CAR-T programsPfizer entered into an exclusive licensing agreement with Starna Therapeutics under which Starna is set to receive an upfront payment of $330 million and is eligible for up to $2.3 billion in milestone payments tied to development and commercial milestones, plus royalties on net sales of approved products.2Under the agreement, Pfizer obtains exclusive rights outside Greater China to develop, manufacture and commercialize three pre-IND in vivo chimeric antigen receptor T-cell programs focused on treating autoimmune diseases.2 Pfizer also receives rights to use Starna’s proprietary in vivo CAR-T technology in inflammation and immunology and in oncology, along with options to exclusively license compounds created under a separate research collaboration and an option to expand the territory to include exclusive rights to develop and commercialize each exclusively licensed compound and product in Greater China.2 Pfizer is expected to lead clinical development outside Greater China and plans to manufacture the finished drug product for the initial clinical trials using its facilities in the United States, with sole and exclusive control over commercialization outside Greater China for all products.The Pfizer-Starna deal also fits a broader pattern of large pharma licensing innovative technology out of China, as John Stanford, executive director at Incubate, told Pharmaceutical Executive, “the surge of interest in Chinese licensing is the product of two decades of deliberate investment. China had a very stated objective — not just to be a cheap supplier, but to edge into innovative industries. That investment is now paying off.”Michael Vincent, chief inflammation and immunology officer, Pfizer, says “In vivo CAR-T is an emerging and promising approach for treating autoimmune diseases, and the patients who might benefit most are those for whom today’s options fall short. Pfizer has significant experience in developing and manufacturing RNA-based medicines globally, and Starna’s in vivo CAR-T programs and technology give us a powerful way to pursue these approaches.”SourcesVerismo Therapeutics Licenses In Vivo CAR T Engineering Technology to Extend Its Novel Multi-Chain KIR-CAR Platform verismo Therapeutics November 18, 2026, https://www.prnewswire.com/news-releases/verismo-therapeutics-licenses-in-vivo-car-t-engineering-technology-to-extend-its-novel-multi-chain-kir-car-platform-302943157.htmlPfizer Enters into Exclusive Licensing Agreement with Starna Therapeutics for Autoimmune Diseases Pfizer November 18, 2026, https://www.pfizer.com/news/press-release/press-release-detail/pfizer-enters-exclusive-licensing-agreement-starna Newsletter Lead with insight with the Pharmaceutical Executive newsletter, featuring strategic analysis, leadership trends, and market intelligence for biopharma decision-makers. title: STAT Plus: Merck, Isomorphic Labs partner to develop oncology drug candidates
content: STAT PlusExclusive Merck, Isomorphic Labs partner to develop oncology drug candidates Collaboration will focus on small molecules aimed at undisclosed oncology target Manage alerts for this article Save this story for later Share this article Adobe By Katherine MacPhailNov. 19, 2026 Reporter, Live Journalism Katherine MacPhail[email protected]Katherine MacPhail is a reporter and editorial events programmer for STAT. Merck and Isomorphic Labs, the artificial intelligence drug designer built on a Nobel winning technology that can model how molecules will bind to proteins, said Thursday that they are entering into a research collaboration to discover small molecule candidates for an undisclosed oncology target of “strategic importance.” The partnership — only the latest such deal between a pharma giant and Isomorphic — will bring together the latter’s proprietary drug design engine and existing wet lab data from Merck, officials from both companies said. Merck will handle the preclinical and clinical development, manufacturing, and commercializing of any products. Advertisement “It is a target of high interest to us, a target where we have deployed internal efforts, and we think the pairing of those datasets with the Isomorphic drug discovery engine technology could be a very powerful pairing,” said George Addona, global head of discovery, preclinical development, and translational medicine at Merck. content: STAT PlusNewsletterPharmalot Pharmalittle: We’re reading about a Merck AI deal, China and the pharma supply chain, and more FDA approves a Sanofi drug for a ‌genetic condition affecting the brain and nervous system Manage alerts for this article Save this story for later Share this article Alex Hogan/STAT By Ed SilvermanNov. 19, 2026 Pharmalot Columnist, Senior Writer Ed Silverman[email protected]Ed’s stories explore prescription drug pricing, affordability and access, as well issues surrounding patents, litigation, and legislation. He is also the author of the morning Pharmalittle newsletter and the afternoon Pharmalot newsletter. Rise and shine, everyone, another busy day is on the way. And it is getting off to a pleasant start here on the Pharmalot campus, where clear blue skies and comfy breezes are greeting us. As for the official mascots, they have finished keeping passersby at bay and are now happily snoozing in their respective corners. As for us, we are firing up the trusty kettle for another cup of stimulation. Our choice today is peppermint, an old standby from our pantry. Of course, you are invited to join us. Meanwhile, here is the latest menu of tidbits. As always, do keep in touch. And best of luck today. … Merck and Isomorphic Labs, the artificial intelligence drug designer built on a Nobel-winning technology that can model how molecules will bind to proteins, are entering into a research collaboration to discover small molecule candidates for an undisclosed oncology target of “strategic importance,” STAT reports. The partnership — only the latest such deal between a pharma giant and Isomorphic — will join Isomorphic’s proprietary drug design engine and existing wet lab data from Merck, which will handle the preclinical and clinical development, manufacturing, and commercializing of any products. Advertisement The U.S. Food and Drug Administration approved a Sanofi drug, making ​it the first treatment for a ‌type of rare genetic condition that affects the brain and nervous system, Reuters writes. The drug, ​branded as Infilbray, was approved for ​adults and children weighing at least ⁠15 kilograms, or about 33 pounds, ​with type 3 Gaucher disease, a ​rare inherited disorder that causes fatty substances to build up in the body and brain. The ​approval was based on a late-stage ​study of 43 patients aged 12 years and ‌older ⁠whose symptoms outside the brain and nervous system had been stabilized with enzyme replacement therapy.
